subject: openhands
title: Faux-provider full-stack E2E: scripted OpenAI-compatible server drives the real agent runtime against the built UI in CI
one_why: Nuance vs the 4 existing faux-provider findings: the fake LLM is the SDK's own TestLLM replaying trajectories incl. injected auth/rate-limit/context-window faults, so CI exercises real runtime + real error paths with zero provider spend; convergence signal.

subject: openhands
title: Live-LLM end-to-end conversation runs on PRs, credential-gated and fork-excluded
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:106-295 (run :265-276), .github/workflows/ci.yml:149-151 (skip fork PRs so secrets never reach untrusted code)
one_why: Nuance vs 4 prior evals-in-ci: this is acceptance-grade (asserts expected reply/bash tokens with a live model, posts video artifacts), not a scored eval suite - but it is the corpus's first workflow-file evidence clearing the anchor errata's verification-9 bar.

subject: openhands
title: CI-executed lint-as-architecture: a unit test bans ad-hoc HTTP to the backend outside an allowlist
one_why: Walks all of src/ and fails if any file uses the shared axios instance or raw fetch to the agent server - the typed-client boundary is a compiled-and-tested invariant, not a convention; trivially portable to our repo.

subject: openhands
title: Client tool lets the agent steer the human's UI: server executor is a no-op, frontend dispatches canvas_ui_control actions
one_why: Reverse of every other subject's UI: the agent opens tabs, navigates to files, and shows previews in the user's browser via action events the client consumes; legacy events stay resolvable for persisted conversations - a copyable pattern for agent-directed workspace focus.

subject: openhands
title: Agent-triggered child conversations with isolation enum and a corruption-tolerant local launch ledger
one_why: Reused id: the UI-side half is new - localStorage ledger keyed by parent ('a corrupt ledger must not block the launch'), cloud-sandbox polling with fixed cadence/ceiling, and isolation levels per child; result attribution survives UI reload.

subject: openhands
title: Product surfaces render only what an admitted extension manifest declares - no manifest, no nav entries, routes 404
one_why: Host holds zero automation-specific copy, endpoints, or attributes itself; the pinned extensions package publishes them and admission validation gates rendering - contract-first UI that keeps deep links honest.

subject: openhands
title: Multi-backend registry: one shell drives local/remote/cloud agent servers and different agents per backend, with version-compat gating
one_why: Health probing, per-backend agent_kind, min-version handshake with 401-sentinel detection, and a dedicated 850-LOC cross-backend E2E - the strongest rival-harness-import surface found (Claude Code/Codex/Gemini via ACP on any backend).

subject: openhands
title: Deployment docs state the threat model bluntly, and extension spec states what its guards do NOT guard
one_why: 'Anyone who can talk to the agent server can read/write the FS, exec, network - treat the VM as a machine holding production credentials'; extension consent split is explicitly labeled 'product consent invariant, not proof of human presence against an agent with the same APIs' - the honesty the rubric rewards, in doc form.

subject: openhands
title: Approval policy is composed client-side from settings; default is NeverConfirm, enforcement lives in the backend
one_why: Reused id: settings → {kind: NeverConfirm | ConfirmRisky(threshold HIGH, confirm_unknown) | AlwaysConfirm} plus LLM/pattern/policy-rail analyzer selection, tested - but the shell's own default posture requires opt-in approval, and nothing in this tree binds the agent.

subject: openhands
title: MCP tool results and error text are scrubbed of configured secrets before reaching the UI
one_why: Secret values from MCP server configs are redacted from echoed tool_result/error text with round-trip substitution on write-back - prevents credential leakage into chat logs/renderers, a gap in every other subject so far.

subject: openhands
title: npm package ships a real process supervisor for its polyglot stack: shutdown-hook registry, port leases, stable 0600 keys, file logs
one_why: uvx-pinned Python backends + static frontend + ingress behind one origin, with SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP cleanup, lease semantics for parallel stacks, and a single source of truth for version pins - how a CLI-only agent could learn to ship a multi-process product.

subject: openhands
title: Stryker mutation testing and an affected-E2E router exist but no workflow invokes either
evidence: stryker.config.mjs:1-12; package.json scripts test:mutation:diff; tests/e2e/mock-llm/test-mapping.json + tests/e2e/mock-llm/scripts/resolve-affected-tests.mjs (no .github/ reference)
one_why: Both are wired to human hands only - mutation runs are not in CI and the router that could scope mock-LLM E2E to changed areas is unreferenced, so every push-to-main pays for the full suite while regressions slip through PRs; cheap fix, visible in repo archaeology.
